Recommendation: refuse. Do not size this one.

Net flow is essentially flat (+3.3 SOL on 89.7 SOL bought), so buyers are not absorbing the sell pressure. The launch bot presence and the 0.24 completer share are not reassuring either. Pool depth of 76 SOL means a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% cost is manageable, but depth does not fix the momentum or distribution picture.

If the desk overrides and buys anyway, the most defensible parameters would be $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. Any stop-out or failed bounce should exit immediately.

Refuse any size if the pool falls below roughly 50 SOL, if sells exceed buys over the next 10 minutes, or if the price breaks below the current level without a volume recovery.

Buyer count is high (388) and the last 15 minutes show real two-sided activity with $21k volume and 241 buyers, with a slight positive net flow (+3.31 SOL) and a +3% return. Pool depth of 76 SOL is reasonable for a $20 ticket.

But the demand signal is weak. Net flow is nearly flat against heavy churn: 86 SOL sold versus 90 SOL bought, and the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.86. The coin is down 59% from its 30-minute high and 20% over 30 minutes, and buyers are still being outnumbered by sellers in the recent window. A launch bot was present, which is a red flag for early price action. Nothing in the brief shows demand accelerating; it shows a coin already past its peak, bleeding, with flat flow.

Verdict: no clear case to buy. Skip.
memos.skeptic:

The coin is down 59% from its 30-minute high, and the last 15 minutes show $21.2k volume with 86.4 SOL sold against 89.7 SOL bought, so net flow is roughly flat (+3.3 SOL) and the +3% return is a thin bounce on heavy two-way churn. Sellers (201) nearly match buyers (241), which looks like holders exiting into demand rather than new conviction.

Launch-phase structure is weak: the first 2 minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.86 and a launch bot present, and the completer took 23.6% of the curve. Pool depth is only 76 SOL, so a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% cost is slim against any hourly move, and a single sell wall would move price more than the fees.

The offsetting positives (ORGANIC class, low bundle share, top-3 at 7%) don't cancel the -20% 30-minute return and the 59% drawdown. Skip.
